skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill does the stated cloud video analysis, but it also links analyses to identifiers, retrieves cloud history, and silently manages/stores account tokens in ways users should review first.

dimensions.detail: Pet drying-box video analysis is coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifacts also include cloud history retrieval and generic API methods for page/list/add/edit/delete that go beyond simple analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The manifest instructs automatic history-report queries on broad keywords and tells the agent to read an api-key/open-id from local skill or shared config before asking the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution or package-install script was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though the bundled common module is broad.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending user-provided videos or URLs to a remote analysis service is expected for this skill and disclosed, but the identifier-linked cloud history access and account workflow are high-impact and under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The shared utility can silently register/login an identifier, attach tokens to outbound requests, and store token/open_token values in a local SQLite database; a hardcoded api-key-like value is also present in shared config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local videos or public video URLs being sent to the LifeEmergence cloud service and with reports being tied to an open-id, username, or phone-like identifier. Review the bundled config and token storage behavior first, because the skill can create/login an account and store returned tokens locally for later API calls.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the scope concern: history report retrieval and broad record-management methods are present beyond the declared video-analysis workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the identifier/credential concern: local config open-id lookup, username/phone collection, silent phoneLogin/register, and local token persistence are present.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The nested analysis API documentation contains an unrelated face/constitution diagnosis response, which creates real capability-contract ambiguity even though the top-level reference names heat-stress endpoints.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The manifest's history-query auto-trigger keywords can invoke cloud history access without a clearly separated confirmation step.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote upload/API processing is expected for server-side video analysis and is disclosed in the description, but account-linked transmission and retention details are not clearly explained.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The concern is supported because historical reports are retrieved by an open-id/username/phone-like identifier and the skill prioritizes reading that identifier from local config.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic DAO filtering exists, but it appears to be a generic local helper and is not the main reason for Review without evidence that untrusted users can directly control those filters.
